title: Connector erasure re-drive is unbounded against concurrency — and all three prescribed fixes are blocked (QA F-6)
description:
**BLUF — QA F-6. The connector erasure re-drive SELECT is unbounded against concurrency, and all THREE of the fixes prescribed for it are blocked by something measurable. Filing rather than half-building one, because each of the three fails in a way that is worse than the defect.**

The race (`services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`): the re-drive read

```sql
SELECT id FROM data_subject_requests
WHERE user_id = $1::uuid AND type = 'erasure'
  AND status NOT IN ('completed', 'denied')
ORDER BY requested_at ASC LIMIT 1
```

takes no lock. Platform S retries **without bound**, so two retries that overlap either both select the same DSR and both drive `executeErasureImpl` against it, or both miss and both file one — the orphan accumulation the re-drive was added to prevent.

### The three prescribed fixes, each measured

**1. Partial unique index — cannot be built on existing data.**

```sql
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX … ON data_subject_requests (user_id)
  WHERE type = 'erasure' AND status NOT IN ('completed','denied');
```

Measured on the local database: **4 users already hold more than one non-terminal erasure DSR.** The index would fail to build. (Control: the same GROUP BY … HAVING count(*) > 1 without the type/status predicate returns **12**, so the query discriminates and the 4 is not a false zero.) This needs a data-reconciliation migration first — deciding which duplicate survives is a GDPR-records question, not an index.

**2.** `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` **— wrong for this shape.** If the row is locked by a concurrent attempt, SKIP LOCKED returns nothing, so the second caller falls through to the `else` branch and **files a new DSR**. That is precisely the accumulation the re-drive block exists to prevent, and the comment above it says so. Plain blocking `FOR UPDATE` is the right semantic, but it is inert outside an explicit transaction — a single `$queryRaw` commits immediately and drops the lock.

**3.** `prisma.$transaction` **+** `pg_advisory_xact_lock` **— deadlocks on the connection pool.** Transaction-scoped is the correct lock kind here (`pgbouncer.ini:54` is `pool_mode = transaction`, so a session-scoped advisory lock would leak onto whichever client next receives the server connection). But the block it would have to wrap calls `createDSR`, and `createDSR` issues its INSERT on the **module-level** `prisma` (`gdprService.ts:289`), not on the `tx` handle. So the inner write runs on a *different* connection, outside the transaction — losing the atomicity the lock was for — and worse, the outer transaction holds one pooled server connection while the inner call waits for another from the same pool. Under load that is a self-deadlock.

### What a real fix needs

Any of these, and each is its own piece of work:

* Thread a transaction client through `createDSR` (and `writePii`, which it awaits) so the claim and the INSERT share one connection — then the advisory lock works as intended; **or**
* an optimistic claim using the status vocabulary that already exists: a single atomic `UPDATE … SET status='processing' WHERE … AND status='pending' RETURNING id`, where losing the claim means another attempt is in flight. This needs a staleness timeout, or a crashed attempt strands the DSR in `processing` forever; **or**
* reconcile the 4 duplicate rows, then add the partial unique index and have the caller catch `23505` and re-read.

### Scope note

Not shipped in #790. That PR closes QA F-1 (denied DSRs re-driven) and F-5 (a test asserting its own fixture), both Majors, and adding a half-bounded lock would have made the concurrency story *look* handled while leaving the deadlock in. The re-drive block itself is not a regression from #790 — it was added in that PR's earlier revision and the unboundedness is inherent to the shape, not to the KS-695 change.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against branch `feature/ks-695-ask1-erasure-by-external-ref` at `b8d658d2a`, `develop` at `0e67228df`. Duplicate counts and the control read from the local Postgres read-only; `pool_mode` read from `docker/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini:54` and confirmed inside the running `secuura-pgbouncer` container. No writes.

nodes.body:
**BLUF:** Kam ruled the 31-decision card `secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109` on 2026-11-09 at 13:44:07 (live board), in these words: "Decision secuura-backlog-31-decisions-1109: a — All recommendations (A and B)". Option a reads: "Every row ruled as recommended; a board seat files and moves the tickets; the KS-607 demo rows still wait for a separate yes." This ticket is row A12 of the decision pack, ruled as recommended: option 1. One atomic claim step using the statuses that already exist, plus a timeout for claims left behind by a crash. It needs no ruling on GDPR records and cannot deadlock the connection pool.

A build seat does the work; nothing was changed in code by this comment.

Alongside this comment the ticket moves from Backlog to Todo.

## The two gdpr erasure endpoints came off the schemathesis failing set — measured, not fixed here

`GET /api/gdpr/erasures/{externalRef}` and `POST /api/gdpr/erasures` failed in **every** pre-rebuild run (s152 12:12Z, and two more at 12:57Z / 13:00Z) and passed in **every** post-rebuild run (13:05Z / 13:07Z), on the same commit `5ffaaf396` — so the fix was already in the code and a stale local image was hiding it.

⚠ **This does NOT say this ticket is done.** The measurement separates old code from new code, not one commit from another, and the erasure family spans KS-695 / KS-754 / KS-757 / KS-758. Attributing the change to any one of them needs a bisect that was not run.

Full cells and controls on **KS-695**. *(s153, 2026-09-08.)*
